applies_to.notes: Includes mucinous and signet-ring cell subtypes.

applies_to.histology: Squamous cell carcinoma of the colon/rectum
applies_to.notes: Primary colorectal squamous cell carcinoma, not anal canal squamous cell carcinoma.
Small cell and large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma; staged using this colorectal carcinoma system per AJCC 8th.

does_not_apply_to.reason: Staged separately per AJCC due to distinct anatomy/biology and its own T category definitions.

does_not_apply_to.histology: Well-differentiated neuroendocrine tumor (carcinoid) of the colon/rectum
does_not_apply_to.reason: Staged using the separate AJCC neuroendocrine tumor (NET) staging system, not the colorectal carcinoma system.
Anatomically and biologically distinct (HPV-related squamous cell carcinoma predominant); staged using the separate AJCC anal carcinoma system.

does_not_apply_to.histology: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST) of the colon/rectum
does_not_apply_to.reason: Mesenchymal tumor staged using the separate AJCC GIST staging system.

8th.reference: AJCC Cancer Staging Manual, 8th Edition (2017), Chapter 20: Colon and Rectum, pp. 251-274.

t_categories.description: Carcinoma in situ, intramucosal carcinoma (involvement of lamina propria with no extension through muscularis mucosae).
Tumor invades the submucosa (through the muscularis mucosae but not into the muscularis propria).
Tumor invades through the muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissues.
Tumor invades the visceral peritoneum or invades or adheres to adjacent organ or structure

Tumor invades through the visceral peritoneum (including gross perforation of the bowel through tumor and continuous invasion of tumor through areas of inflammation to the surface of the visceral peritoneum).
Tumor directly invades or is adherent to other organs or structures.

n_categories.description: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed.
Metastasis in 1-3 regional lymph nodes (tumor in lymph node measuring ≥0.2 mm), or any number of tumor deposits are present and all identifiable lymph nodes are negative.
One regional lymph node is positive.
Two or three regional lymph nodes are positive.
No regional lymph nodes are positive, but tumor deposits are present in the subserosa, mesentery, or non-peritonealized pericolic/perirectal tissues.
Metastasis in 4 or more regional lymph nodes, without further subclassification into N2a or N2b as documented.
Four to six regional lymph nodes are positive.
Seven or more regional lymph nodes are positive.

m_categories.description: No distant metastasis detected on imaging or exam; no evidence of tumor in distant organs/sites.
Distant metastasis identified, without further subclassification into M1a, M1b, or M1c as documented.
Metastasis to one site or organ is identified without peritoneal metastasis.
Metastasis to two or more sites or organs is identified without peritoneal metastasis.
Metastasis to the peritoneal surface is identified alone or with other site or organ metastases.

t_categories.description: Carcinoma in situ, intramucosal carcinoma (involvement of lamina propria with no extension through muscularis mucosae).
Tumor invades the submucosa (through the muscularis mucosae but not into the muscularis propria).
Tumor invades through the muscularis propria into pericolorectal tissues.
Tumor invades through the visceral peritoneum and/or directly invades or is adherent to other organs or structures, without further subclassification into T4a or T4b as documented.

Tumor invades through the visceral peritoneum (including gross perforation of the bowel through tumor and continuous invasion of tumor through areas of inflammation to the surface of the visceral peritoneum).

Tumor directly invades or is adherent to other organs or structures, confirmed on microscopic examination of the resection specimen, or, for tumors adherent to other organs/structures macroscopically, microscopic confirmation of invasion beyond the layer of the bowel wall.

n_categories.description: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed.
No regional lymph node metastasis, confirmed on histologic examination of the resected specimen (recommended minimum of 12 nodes examined).
Metastasis in 1-3 regional lymph nodes (tumor in lymph node measuring ≥0.2 mm), or any number of tumor deposits are present and all identifiable lymph nodes are negative.
One regional lymph node is positive on histologic examination.
Two or three regional lymph nodes are positive on histologic examination.
No regional lymph nodes are positive, but tumor deposits are present in the subserosa, mesentery, or non-peritonealized pericolic/perirectal tissues, identified on histologic examination.
Metastasis in 4 or more regional lymph nodes, without further subclassification into N2a or N2b as documented.
Four to six regional lymph nodes are positive on histologic examination.
Seven or more regional lymph nodes are positive on histologic examination.

m_categories.description: No distant metastasis identified on pathologic review (pM0 is not assignable from resection of the primary alone without pathologic confirmation elsewhere; used when biopsy/resection of a distant site confirms absence, otherwise M category is derived clinically).
Distant metastasis identified, without further subclassification into M1a, M1b, or M1c as documented.
Metastasis to one site or organ is identified, confirmed microscopically, without peritoneal metastasis.
Metastasis to two or more sites or organs is identified, confirmed microscopically, without peritoneal metastasis.
Metastasis to the peritoneal surface is identified, confirmed microscopically, alone or with other site or organ metastases.
